title: Schema-handshake + timeboxed streaming acceptance with graceful tool-call recovery
creator: Priya Singh
description: PRD/Acceptance checklist for a new runtime protocol that: (1) negotiates a minimal schema handshake before streaming structured payloads, (2) enforces timeboxed chunk emission and clear partial-object boundaries, and (3) defines deterministic, idempotent tool/function-call retry and graceful-recovery behaviors when downstream tool invocations fail. Goal: implement a single, testable contract that production services (hosted + dedicated + private) can adopt without breaking existing non-streaming clients.
acceptance_criteria: Schema handshake: client or server must include a single-line JSON 'schema_envelope' at stream start ("schema_version", "required_fields") or the server will return a 400 with code 'schema-missing'. Implementation must support fallback parsing when schema_version == "legacy".

Streaming envelope rules: all streamed payloads MUST be newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) where each line is either 'progress', 'partial_object', 'complete_object', or 'tool_call' envelope. Parsers must be able to recover on incomplete final line until the connection closes.

Partial-object semantics: when emitting partial_object lines, the runtime must include an explicit 'continuation_id' and 'byte_offset' fields. A complete_object must reference the same 'continuation_id' and have cumulative 'byte_offset' >= last offset.

Timeboxed chunk guarantee: the runtime must emit a token chunk or envelope at least once every 200ms for low-latency customers when 'latency_mode' is 'snappy'. If no content is available, emit a 'heartbeat' envelope with 'heartbeat_seq' to preserve parser liveness.

Tool-call handshake: tool_call envelopes must include 'tool_id', 'call_id', 'input_digest' (sha256 hex), and 'idempotency_key'. The platform must not invoke the external tool more than once per unique 'idempotency_key' within a 5-minute window (configurable).

Tool-call failure modes: the runtime must classify failures into: 'tool-timeout', 'tool-error' (non-2xx), 'tool-parse-failure'. For 'tool-timeout' the runtime should retry once with exponential backoff; for 'tool-error' the runtime should return a deterministic fallback (see fallbacks criterion); for 'tool-parse-failure' the runtime must emit a 'tool_diagnostic' envelope containing first 2KB of tool output redacted for PII.

Fallback behavior: projects must specify a fallback model/action. On repeated tool failures (>2), the system should fallback to either (a) a cached tool response if available, (b) a model-only response with a 'fallback_reason' field, or (c) a structured error envelope with guidance for client retry. The acceptance tests must include at least one scenario for each fallback option.

Idempotency & dedup: the platform must expose a deterministic mapping from (call_id, idempotency_key) to invocation state. Duplicate envelopes received by the runtime for the same call must not trigger a new tool invocation and must return the original outcome/shadow result.

Backpressure and graceful close: when the client signals 'pause' or the runtime detects downstream congestion, the runtime may emit a 'paused' envelope and must resume deterministically on 'resume'. On unresolved congestion for >30s, emit a 'stream_terminated' envelope with reason and an idempotent resume token.

Compatibility: non-streaming clients (single-response API) must continue to work. If a client requests 'stream=false' the runtime must validate schema but return a single JSON envelope identical in shape to the reconstructed NDJSON stream.

Observability: every stream must generate structured telemetry: 'schema_version', 'latency_mode', 'tool_calls.count', 'tool_calls.failures', 'partial_emits.count', and 'stream_duration_ms'. Dashboards and alerts (P90 stream error rate >1%) must be provisioned before rollout.

Security & PII redaction: tool diagnostic payloads must be redacted via our KMS-assisted PII-scrubber prior to being included in envelopes, and the acceptance harness must validate that no PII regex hits are present in emitted diagnostics.

E2E correctness: for 10 canonical test prompts (provided in test set) the streamed reconstruction must match the non-streamed ground truth JSON object exactly (byte-equal) for both happy path and single partial-recovery retry scenarios.

Rollout constraint: feature gated behind 'streaming_schema_v2' flag. Canary must be limited to 5% traffic, for at least 48 hours with no P0 errors, before 25% ramp. SLO target: streaming end-to-end p95 latency < 1.2x non-streamed baseline for matched requests.
Docs & SDKs: Node/Python SDKs must include parser helpers that expose a high-level iterator over complete objects and tool-call event hooks before GA.
Acceptance tests must be deterministic and runnable in CI without external network access by using test doubles for all tool integrations.
tests: Unit: schema_envelope parser with legacy/unknown versions (100% coverage of branch matrix)
Integration: simulated tool that returns 200/500/timeout/invalid-json to validate retry and fallback logic
E2E: CI job 'streaming_schema_v2_e2e' which reconstructs streamed NDJSON into final JSON and compares byte-equal to golden files
Load: 10k concurrent short-lived streams (latency_mode=snappy) to validate heartbeat and timeboxed emission under load
Security: automated PII scanner against tool_diagnostic payloads in acceptance harness
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Agreed to use NDJSON (line-delimited) vs interleaved json chunks to improve parser recovery (decision by Alex, Priya, and Rafael).
2026-03-12: Chose 'single retry then fallback' policy for tool-timeout after benchmarking 10ms median tool latency (Trade-off: reduces flakiness at expense of slightly increased tail latency).
2026-03-13: Decided to expose idempotency_key as required for all tool calls to simplify dedup across private deployments (security & audit benefit).
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created. Initial draft PRD and acceptance checklist attached.
